slides.title: What a Digital Opinion Leader Is
bullets: An HCP, researcher, or patient advocate with real scientific influence online
Active on LinkedIn, ResearchGate, blogs, podcasts, digital communities
Perceived by their audience as a credible scientific source
Complements and often overlaps with the traditional KOL

slides.title: The Channel Changes, Not Necessarily the Expertise
bullets: Many leading KOLs are also active DOLs
A KOL influences through publications, congresses, personal ties
A DOL extends that influence into digital communities
Digital reach often means broader, younger, more dispersed audiences

slides.title: Mapping DOLs Takes a Different Process
bullets: Social listening to see who drives real engagement
Co-authorship and citation analysis to verify scientific solidity
MSL field insight on who the local community follows online
Congress visibility often signals associated digital activity

slides.title: Followers Are Not the Same as Influence
bullets: Anchoring bias: visibility gets confused with scientific influence
Follower count and posting frequency are not credibility
Reach and rigor don't always move together
Apply the same critical thinking used to evaluate any evidence

slides.title: The Starting Point for This Module
bullets: Understanding DOLs comes before designing digital content or channels
Sets up how content and metrics get tailored to this audience

takeaway.title: A DOL earns scientific influence online, and reach alone doesn't prove it
bullets: DOLs and KOLs can overlap, but their channels and audiences differ
Mapping a DOL means checking social listening against real scientific rigor
Visibility without credibility is a bias trap to avoid
